rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine decree does not cancel human partial will: voluntary acts occurring through that will are themselves included in qadar.
rows.anchor: “Kader” abdin irâde-i cüz’iyesine münâfî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creative command is qadar's enactment by qada, bringing creation and action into being.
rows.anchor: O halk ve fiilin nasıl olduğuna, yani kaderin kazâ ile icrâsına gelince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's decree is effected by one instantaneous command, like a blink; as in 36:82, the complete cause makes its effect occur at once, so resurrection and the Hour are certain.
rows.anchor: Hakikatte illet-i tâmme bu kün emridir. İllet vâki‘olunca ma‘lul de hemen olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of earlier communities like the present audience should make them realize that they too are on the way to destruction and reflect.
rows.anchor: Hem emsâlinizi hep helâk etmişizdir düşünseniz siz de gitmek üzere bulunduğunuzu anlarsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed, small or great, is recorded; after death a person's future is the yield of worldly acts, weighed by God and determining the resurrection.
rows.anchor: insanın helâkten sonra da bir istikbâli vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing, those protected from disbelief and disobedience, are in gardens and a flow of light.
rows.anchor: şüphesiz ki müttakīler küfr ü isyandan korunanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although nahr first suggests a river, Elmalılı prefers the sense of daylight, light and brightness, glossing it as a current of light.
rows.anchor: “neher”, “nehr” gibi ırmak mânasına olmak mütebâdir görünürse de “nehâr” maddesinden nûr ve aydınlık mânasına olmak daha latiftir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maq'ad sidq is the seat or assembly of truth: a fixed station for the truthful, incapable of proving false or passing away.
rows.anchor: sâdıklara mahsus olan ve yalan çıkması, zevâl bulması ihtimâli olmayan sâbit bir makam ve mevkide

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The powerful sovereign in whose presence the righteous dwell is God, the Most Merciful; the tanwīn in both names marks grandeur.
rows.anchor: gayet iktidarlı, yani kudretine nihâyet olmayan bir melîkin, pek büyük mülk sâhibi bir şehinşâhın huzûr-ı kibriyâsında ki Rahmân teâlâ’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports an unnamed view that the indefinite wording of divine nearness and the two names signals ungraspable dominion and power, and an indescribably great bliss and honor in God's presence.
rows.anchor: Demişlerdir ki Hak sübhânehû burada indiyet ve kurbü

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says some transmitted reports give these two divine names a special status in having supplications answered.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Bazı eserlerde vârid olduğuna göre

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Müseyyeb
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Shayba transmits Sa'id b. al-Musayyab's account: after a frightening nighttime encounter in the mosque, he was told to invoke God as Malik Muqtadir and ask; thereafter his requests were granted.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Şeybe Sa‘îd b. Müseyyeb’den tahric etmiştir, demiş ki: “Mescide girdim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the phrase as two further gardens lying beyond the preceding ones.
rows.anchor: Ötelerinden de diğer cennetân (62).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the gardens as intensely dark green, calling them lush and verdant.
rows.anchor: Yağız yeşil ne dilsitân (64).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tams originally means bleeding, especially menstrual bleeding; it came to mean intercourse with a virgin and, some say, intercourse generally, so the women are untouched and virginal.
rows.anchor: “Tams” esasen kanamaktır, onun için hayız kanına “tams” denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward for goodness is goodness: beautiful recompense for good action; this implies that the earlier fear means acting with ihsan.
rows.anchor: Bundan anlaşılır ki yukarıda “havf”tan murad ihsan ile ameldir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan is worshipping God as though one sees Him, while knowing that He sees the worshipper if unseen.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfinde îzah olunduğu üzere Allah’ı görüyormuşsun gibi

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: In a report from Anas, the Prophet explains the verse as saying that the one whom God has blessed with tawhid receives no reward except Paradise.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Enes’ten rivayetlerinde Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem işbu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considered broadly to include both knowledge and practice, tawhid falls within the hadith's meaning of ihsan.
rows.anchor: Tevhid, ilmî ve amelîden e‘am olarak mülâhaza edilince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the verse is more evidently read broadly, joining the two occurrences of ihsan in a general sense.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh âyette iki ihsânı mefhûmen birleştirmek için daha umûmî olarak tefsir edilmesi zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the first pair of gardens with the foremost brought near to God, and the second pair with the companions of the right.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den mervî olduğuna göre evvelkiler

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan's reported view assigns the first gardens to the forerunners and the later ones to their followers.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan mervî olduğuna göre evvelkiler sâbıkīn, sonrakiler tâbi‘în içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On those views, the second gardens are lower in rank: the first are more comprehensive and perfected in their branching qualities, expressing the highest degree of ihsan.
rows.anchor: Bunlara göre ikinciler kadr ü mertebece evvelkilerden aşağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some instead hold that the later gardens have more praiseworthy qualities, making min dūnihimā mean beyond or further on from the first pair.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh bazıları sonrakilerin evsâfı daha memduh olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhāmmatān is a feminine dual participial form from the intensive verb of darkening; from duhma, it evokes night-darkness or a dark bay horse and here denotes deep, almost black green.
rows.anchor: Aslı “dühme”den gelir ki gece karaltısı veya

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Ata and others gloss mudhāmmatān as khadrāwān, green.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, İbn Cübeyr, İkrime, Atâ, İbn Ebî Rebâh ve daha sâirleri “hadrâvân” diye tefsir etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: Abu Ayyub asked the Prophet about the phrase, and the Prophet explained it as green.
rows.anchor: kavl-i ilâhîsinden sordum, Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm ‘hadrâvân’ buyurdu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description emphasizes the intensity of the gardens' greenery, like Turkish yemyeşil or gömgök.
rows.anchor: Demek ki murad yeşilliklerinin kuvvetini beyandır. Lisânımızda “yemyeşil” yahut “gömgök” tâbir ederiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadh means water's effusion or gushing, while the dotted form nadhkh is stronger; the phrase depicts bubbling or spraying fountains.
rows.anchor: “Nadh” (نَضْح) suyun feverânı, püskürmesidir. Nokta ile nadh نَضْخ ise daha kuvvetlisidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some consider these fountain springs more artful, beautiful and perfected than the flowing springs described at 55:50.
rows.anchor: bunları عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ’dan daha memduh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite forms magnify fruits beyond anything familiar; dates and pomegranates are singled out for food and medicinal qualities, with seedless pomegranate especially notable.
rows.anchor: “Fâkihe”den sonra bilhassa “nahl” ile “rummân”ın zikri de Sûre-i En‘âm’da geçtiği üzere bunların yemişlikten başka ta‘âm ve devâ itibariyle de bir husûsiyetleri olmasındandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women are good and beautiful in both character and physical form, beneficial as well as comely.
rows.anchor: İçlerinde hayırlı güzeller, yani ahlâkları da güzel hilkatleri de güzel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūr is the plural of ahwar or hawra, describing doe-eyed beauty with intensely white sclera and intensely black pupils.
rows.anchor: “Hûr” “ahver”in veya “havrâ”nın cem‘idir ki gözünün beyazı şiddetle beyaz, karası da şiddetle kara olan âhu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hūr are distinguished, sheltered women residing in their own tents, not a group wandering about.
rows.anchor: haymeler içinde maksur hûriler yani şurada burada dolaşan takımdan değil, evlerinin işiyle meşgul muhaddere

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi cites Ibn Abbas and Umm Salama's report from the Prophet interpreting hūr as bīḍ, white women.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “İbn Münzir ve gayrilerinin İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Umm Salama hadith is established as sound, Elmalılı says one must not depart from the Prophet's interpretation.
rows.anchor: Ümmü Seleme hadîsinin sıhhati sâbit olursa Resûlullah’ın tefsirinden udûl olunmamak lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayme commonly means a tent; dictionaries describe Arab dwellings made as rounded shelters from hair, skins, branches or reeds, with local names for wooden and reed forms.
rows.anchor: “Hayme” lisânımızda çadır diye meşhurdur.

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet describing a heavenly tent as a hollow pearl sixty miles high, with a believer's household at each corner, unseen by the others.
rows.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim, Tirmizî ve daha sâirlerinin Ebû Mûsâ el-Eş‘arî Hazretleri’nden rivayet ettikleri üzere Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den mervîdir

rows.speaker: Ebu’d-Derdâ
rows.claim: Another report from Abu al-Darda describes the heavenly tent as a great pearl with seventy pearl doors.
rows.anchor: Ebu’d-Derdâ Hazretleri’nden rivayete göre hayme bir lü’lüe, büyük bir incidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı treats these descriptions as figurative portrayals of the bliss of heavenly dwellings.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki bunlar cennet meskenlerinin safâsını tasvir için birer temsildir.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says the phrase signals the hūr's honor: they are not imprisoned, but have private tents and curtains prepared as their own dwelling and sleeping space.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “حُورٌۭ مَّقْصُورَٰتٌۭ فِى ٱلْخِيَامِ kavli hûrilerin azametlerine işarettir.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi's subtle reading is that in Paradise things move to the believer: food and drink arrive without his moving, and the hūr are brought in their tents to his palace when desired.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin gösterdiği bu mânadaki letâfeti ifade edebilmek için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To convey Razi's subtle sense, Elmalılı prefers translating hayme as cibinlik, a canopy or bed curtain.
rows.anchor: “cibinlik” ile terceme etmek zevkimizce daha muvâfık olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls the opposition to God and His Messenger the surah's main theme, repeated at its beginning and end.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet işbu Mücâdele Sûresi’nin asıl “mâsîka-leh”ini teşkil eden hedefi demektir. Onun için bu mazmun evvel ve âhirinde tekrar olunacaktır.

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Beydawi explains the opponents as those who deny God's and the Messenger's boundaries, oppose them, or try to prescribe or choose rulings outside those boundaries.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî’nin kısaca beyânına göre Allah ve Resûlünün hudûdunu tanımayıp onlara adâvet eden veya onların tâyin buyurduğu hudûdun gayrı ahkâm vaz‘veya ihtiyar etmeye kalkışan kimseler.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi discusses the limits of the lawmaking authority of those empowered to deliberate and decide; Elmalılı directs readers to his commentary for details.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde bu münasebetle erbâb-ı hall ü akd tarafından kanun vaz‘ve salâhiyetinin hudûdu hakkında bazı tafsîlâtta bulunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı glosses kubitū as being driven back, struck down or toppled face-first while acting arrogantly.
rows.anchor: itildiler, yahut çarpıldılar, yahut tepelendiler ukalâlık taslarken yüzleri üstü kakıldılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs testified to the Prophet's truth, showed the right path and explained the evil of opposing God and His Messenger; disbelievers face humiliating punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in sıdkına delâlet ediyor, doğru yolu gösteriyor, Allah ve Resûlüne karşı gelmenin fenalığını anlatıyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will resurrect them all together and disclose their deeds before witnesses, humiliating and disgracing them.
rows.anchor: yaptıklarını kendilerine haber verecek şâhidler huzurunda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though people have forgotten their deeds, God has counted them one by one and entered them in their records.
rows.anchor: Onlar onu unutmuşlarsa da Allah onu bir bir saymış, defterlerine geçirmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God witnesses everything, and nothing escapes His knowledge.
rows.anchor: Hiçbir şey O’nun ilminden kaçmaz.
